academic_year_covered: Mixed 2026/2027 and 2022/2023 - the official unina.it sources are NOT aligned on one academic year, and this must be understood before using any single field. (1) The orientamento.unina.it course profile is explicitly stamped 'The programme at a glance Updated on a.y. 2026/2027' and already carries the reformed class code 'LM-71 R'. (2) The department programme site (scienzechimiche.unina.it/iccbe) is live-maintained and currently announces 'The selections for A.Y. 2026/2027 will open on the 1st of March', lists the 2026-27 exam calendar and the 2026-27 academic calendar, and names Prof. Vincenzo Russo as Degree Programme Director. (3) The governing teaching regulation (Regolamento Didattico del Corso di Studio) published on scuolapsb.unina.it is dated 31/01/2022 and states 'Regolamento in vigore a partire dall'a.a. 2022-2023'; it still uses the pre-reform class code 'CLASSE LM-71' with no 'R'. (4) The department's own downloadable Student's Guide PDF (LM71_Industrial+Chemistry+for+Circular+and+Bio+Economy_REV2) is MATERIALLY STALE: it still names Prof. Martino Di Serio as Degree Programme Director and Prof. Roberta Marchetti as contact for international students, whereas the live website names Prof. Vincenzo Russo for both roles; it also still says 'The call for applications is issued in late June', which contradicts the live site's 1 March opening. (5) The FEE and ENROLMENT data is fully 2026/2027: the university 'Guida all'iscrizione Anno accademico 2026-27' (dated 10/07/2026) gives the 16 July 2026 - 2 November 2026 ordinary enrolment window and the 2026/27 contribution bands. (6) The international.unina.it admission-regulation page carries the 2026 non-EU dates (pre-enrolment 15 June 2026, visa 30 November 2026) but its fee paragraph is STALE (it still quotes a EUR 140/year regional tax, superseded by the 2026/27 bands of EUR 130 / 151 / 173). Where sources conflict, this file follows the most recently updated official page and flags the conflict in uncertainty_notes.
program_name: Industrial Chemistry for Circular and Bio Economy. Official Italian legal/administrative title, as printed on the header of the teaching regulation published by the Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base: 'REGOLAMENTO DIDATTICO DEL CORSO DI STUDIO INDUSTRIAL CHEMISTRY FOR CIRCULAR AND BIO ECONOMY - CHIMICA INDUSTRIALE PER L'ECONOMIA CIRCOLARE E LA BIOECONOMIA'. The degree is awarded under the ENGLISH name; the Italian name is the parallel administrative denomination. Internal University of Naples Federico II course code: DG8 (the course teaching portal is https://www.corsi.unina.it/DG8/home). Programme acronym used by the department and in its e-mail address: ICCBE (iccbe@unina.it); official social handle 'iccbe.msc'. STRUCTURE: this is a STANDALONE English-taught Master of Science (Laurea Magistrale, 2nd cycle, 120 CFU, 2 years). It is NOT an English curriculum inside an Italian-named programme and NOT the English track of another degree. CRITICAL STRUCTURAL FACT - IT IS AN INTER-UNIVERSITY (JOINT) DEGREE: Art. 1 of the teaching regulation states 'Il Corso di Studio in Industrial Chemistry for Circular Economy e un corso inter-ateneo dell'Universita di Napoli Federico II e del Politecnico di Torino ed afferisce al Dipartimento di Scienze Chimiche della Federico II'. The orientamento.unina.it profile puts it in one line: 'The Master's Degree in Industrial Chemistry for Circular and Bio Economy (LM-71 class) is a joint degree of the University of Naples Federico II and Polytechnic of Turin.' Students therefore study in TWO cities (see campus). Administering structure at Federico II: Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base, Dipartimento di Scienze Chimiche; the partner structure at POLITO is the Department of Applied Science and Technology (DISAT), whose staff (e.g. Prof. Fabio Deorsola, Prof. Marco Piumetti) teach on the programme and may supervise theses. IMPORTANT DISAMBIGUATION: Federico II runs a SECOND, separate degree in the SAME LM-71 class - 'Scienze e tecnologie della chimica industriale' (Sciences and Technologies of Industrial Chemistry), also administered by the Department of Chemical Sciences but taught in ITALIAN and NOT a joint degree (unina.it course sheet /-/1484876). Do not conflate the two: only ICCBE is English-taught and only ICCBE is the Federico II-Politecnico di Torino joint degree. NAMING INCONSISTENCY INSIDE THE OFFICIAL REGULATION ITSELF: Art. 1 twice writes the short form 'Industrial Chemistry for Circular Economy' (dropping 'and Bio'), while the document header, Art. 2 and every public page use the full 'Industrial Chemistry for Circular and Bio Economy'. The full form is the operative title. Programme lineage: instituted for a.a. 2022/2023 (regulation approved 31/01/2022, in force from a.a. 2022-2023); teaching started September 2022.
level: master. Second-cycle degree - Italian 'Laurea Magistrale' (2-year Master of Science / MSc). The department's own Student's Guide titles the document '2nd Cycle Master - Industrial Chemistry for Circular and Bio Economy'. Standard duration 2 years / 4 semesters, 120 CFU (ECTS) total. Credit breakdown from the published study plan: FIRST YEAR - one of two alignment paths (Biology path: Bioinorganic Chemistry and Industrial Enzymology 11 CFU + Complements of Microbiology and Biotechnology 10 CFU; OR Chemistry path: Complements of Physical and Analytical Chemistry 11 CFU + Complements of Inorganic and Organic Chemistry 10 CFU), then the common path - Circular Platforms for energy and materials Recovery 10 CFU, Industrial Chemistry 8 CFU, Polymers: production, recycle and characterization 6 CFU, Green Unit Operations 9 CFU, Industrial Biotechnology 7 CFU, plus 3 CFU 'Additional language skills (Italian) or Further knowledge of computer science'. SECOND YEAR - Green plants design 11 CFU, Industrial green simulation process 7 CFU, Elective courses/Challenge 6+6/12 CFU, Traineeship 4 CFU, Thesis 22 CFU. Entry qualification required: an Italian 'Laurea I Livello' (3-year bachelor) or an equivalent foreign first-cycle degree - the orientamento.unina.it fact box states 'Degree required Laurea I Livello'. Final exam: thesis defence before a 5-member Degree Committee appointed by the CCD; graduation grade out of 110 with up to 10/110 awarded for the final examination and 'lode' possible above 110. Minimum thesis duration 5 months. Graduates may sit the State Exam for entry to the Register of the Orders of Chemists and Physicists.
teaching_language: English - 100% of the degree programme. Four independent official statements agree. (1) Teaching regulation Art. 2: 'Il Corso di Laurea Magistrale in Industrial Chemistry for Circular and Bio Economy della classe LM-71 e tenuto in lingua Inglese.' (2) Teaching regulation Art. 7 ('Articolazione delle modalita di insegnamento'): 'L'attivita didattica viene svolta in modalita mista. Il corso di laurea e in lingua inglese.' (3) orientamento.unina.it fact box: 'Language ENG' (a single ENG marking, i.e. no IT/ENG dual marking - contrast with Federico II programmes that are dual-marked). (4) Department site and Student's Guide: 'The Master is taught in English.' ITALIAN IS NOT REQUIRED FOR ADMISSION OR FOR STUDY. international.unina.it states for English-taught programmes: 'If you choose a three-year, five-year or single-cycle degree course in ENGLISH, level B2 Italian language proficiency is not required.' Italian appears in the curriculum only as an OPTIONAL 3 CFU slot - the study plan line reads 'Additional language skills (Italian) or Further knowledge of computer science 3 CFU', i.e. the student may take Italian OR computer science for those 3 credits. Free supplementary Italian is offered but is not part of the degree requirement: the CLA (Centro Linguistico di Ateneo) provides free ICoN self-study online Italian courses at levels A1-C1 to international students ('Participation in the courses is free of charge and the licence is valid for one year'), and the department advertises separate 'ITALIAN LANGUAGE COURSES'. DELIVERY MODE IS PART OF THE LANGUAGE PICTURE: the first semester is delivered in MIXED/BLENDED mode in English - MOOCs on the Federica Web Learning platform (federica.eu), online tutoring via Microsoft Teams, plus compulsory in-person laboratory workshops in January-February that 'can be attended in Naples or Turin'. The regulation caps online credits: 'Il numero massimo di crediti on-line previsti e di 30 CFU.' All subsequent semesters are delivered in presence ('I semestri successivi sono eroganti in presenza' / 'The following semesters are delivered in presence'). Teaching, examinations, the thesis and the thesis defence are all in English; the thesis title page must nonetheless be submitted 'in Italian and English'.
campus: TWO CITIES - this programme is not taught at a single Federico II campus. (A) NAPLES - MONTE SANT'ANGELO. The Federico II home base is the Department of Chemical Sciences at the Complesso Universitario di Monte Sant'Angelo, Via Cintia 21, 80126 Napoli. The orientamento.unina.it 'Places and Links' block states verbatim: 'Site: Universita degli Studi di Napoli Federico II, Complesso Monte Sant'Angelo, via Cintia'; the Student's Guide adds the geographic coordinates '40 50'19.81"N 14 11'06.04"E'. Monte Sant'Angelo is the science/engineering campus in the Fuorigrotta-Soccavo area of western Naples (Line 7 / Cumana rail area), NOT the historic city-centre Corso Umberto complex, NOT Policlinico, NOT Portici and NOT San Giovanni a Teduccio. (B) TURIN - POLITECNICO DI TORINO. Because this is an inter-university joint degree, one full semester is taught in Turin. The orientamento.unina.it study-plan note states verbatim: 'The lectures of second semester of first year will be at Federico II, the lectures of third semester of second year will be taken at Polytechnic of Turin. The second semester of second year is dedicated to the traineeship and thesis which can be done at Federico II, at Polytechnic of Turin or at companies.' SEMESTER-BY-SEMESTER LOCATION MAP: Year 1 Semester 1 = blended/online (MOOC + online tutoring) with compulsory in-person laboratory workshops in January-February attendable EITHER in Naples OR in Turin; Year 1 Semester 2 = in presence at Federico II, Naples (Monte Sant'Angelo); Year 2 Semester 1 (the 'third semester') = in presence at Politecnico di Torino, Turin; Year 2 Semester 2 = traineeship + thesis, at Federico II, at Politecnico di Torino, or at a partner company/research centre. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR APPLICANTS: a student must plan to relocate to Turin for one semester. The department publishes a dedicated 'Staying at PoliTO' section covering POLITO accommodation (Welcome@PoliTO), under-26 discounts on Turin city bus fares, and the certificate that second-year students can request from the POLITO Tax Office/General Secretariat attesting attendance at the Polytechnic (issued against a EUR 16 stamp duty). Support services are likewise dual: UNINA SINAPSI in Naples and the POLITO Special Needs Unit in Turin. NOTE: this field was listed as 'doganlanacak / to be verified' in the research outline; it is now RESOLVED against primary unina.it sources - Monte Sant'Angelo (Naples) plus one semester at Politecnico di Torino.
degree_class: LM-71 R [uncertain - two different official unina.it pages give two different codes]. The orientamento.unina.it course profile, which is stamped 'Updated on a.y. 2026/2027', shows in its fact box: 'Degree class - LM-71 R'. The 'R' suffix marks the RENEWED/reformed degree class introduced by the Italian ministerial reform of degree classes (D.M. 1649/2023), under which pre-reform classes were re-issued with an 'R' code. The underlying class is LM-71 - 'Scienze e tecnologie della chimica industriale' (Sciences and Technologies of Industrial Chemistry). CONFLICTING OFFICIAL SOURCES: the governing teaching regulation on scuolapsb.unina.it (dated 31/01/2022, 'in vigore a partire dall'a.a. 2022-2023') prints 'CLASSE LM-71' with NO 'R', and repeats 'della classe LM-71' in Art. 2; the department's downloadable Student's Guide likewise prints 'Degree programme class: LM-71'; the live department page also says 'of the LM-71 class'. This is a normal transition artefact - the 2022 regulation predates the reform, while the 2026/2027 orientamento sheet reflects the current ministerial coding. The value 'LM-71 R' matches the research outline and is the code to use for a 2026/2027 application; 'LM-71' is the same class pre-reform. No separate ministerial RAD/ordinamento identifier for this course was located on a unina.it page during this research; the SUA-CdS sheet is linked from the department site to the ministerial portal at https://www.universitaly.it/index.php/scheda/sua/59212 (universitaly.it, i.e. MUR, not unina.it).
admission_type: RESTRICTED ACCESS by programme decision, with a capped intake, a compulsory document screening and a compulsory online interview. It is NOT open access, and it is NOT a TOLC, SAT or national numero programmato test. Precise legal basis - teaching regulation Art. 5 ('Modalita per l'accesso al Corso di Studio'): 'La verifica della personale preparazione e obbligatoria in ogni caso, e possono accedervi solo gli studenti in possesso dei requisiti curriculari' and 'L'iscrizione al Corso di Laurea su decisione del CCD puo essere a numero chiuso. Le modalita di selezione degli studenti saranno definite annualmente dalla CCD.' In other words the regulation AUTHORISES a closed number and delegates the annual selection rules to the CCD (Commissione di Coordinamento Didattico); the CCD has in fact set the cap - 'Enrolment is limited to a maximum of 30 participants' (orientamento.unina.it and Student's Guide). The unina.it institutional course card summarises the access mode as 'programmato' and notes that a presentation letter and an interview are required before enrolment. The orientamento.unina.it fact box labels the admission line 'Admission - Verifica di preparazione' (verification of preparation). THE PROCEDURE HAS TWO PARALLEL TRACKS, determined solely by whether the candidate needs an Italian study visa (verbatim from the department page): 'Applicant who don't need a VISA: follow only the internal procedure (a)' and 'Applicant who need a VISA: follow both internal procedure (a) and Universitaly procedure (b)'. (a) INTERNAL PROCEDURE - all applicants complete the department's online selection module (the department publishes it as 'LINK TO THE MODULE FOR THE INTERNAL SELECTION', currently a Google Form at https://forms.gle/XvRE6UtykzTrwPqGA) and upload one single merged PDF named Surname_Name.pdf. The department is categorical that this is the only accepted channel: 'No documents sent in other form (e.g., via email) will be considered.' The candidate is then contacted by e-mail for an online interview. (b) UNIVERSITALY PROCEDURE - visa-needing candidates must ALSO pre-enrol on the ministerial Universitaly portal, selecting 'University of Naples Federico II', leaving the tax code blank if not yet held, and naming the Italian Embassy/Consulate where the visa will be requested. OUTCOME: 'After the colloquium, if the curriculum of the student satisfied the required criteria, the pre-enrollment letter will be: (i) uploaded on Universitaly platform, in case the student need a VISA; (ii) sent to the student, in case the student is already in UE.' IMPORTANT WARNING carried by international.unina.it: 'The University of Naples Federico II does not issue admission letters for obtaining a visa' and 'pre-enrolment alone does not grant admission to degree programmes'.
academic_requirements: A first-cycle degree plus ONE of three curricular routes, PLUS recency and grade filters, PLUS compulsory verification of personal preparation. Entry qualification: 'Laurea I Livello' (Italian 3-year bachelor) or an equivalent foreign first-cycle degree. CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS - verbatim from teaching regulation Art. 4 (Italian) and the department page (English), which match exactly. 'Admission is also permitted if at least 1 of the following curricular requirements is met:' REQUIREMENT 1 - 'Candidates who have graduated in Italy in the Class ex D.M. 270/04: L-27 Chemical Sciences and Technologies' (Italian: 'L-27 Scienze e Tecnologie Chimiche'). REQUIREMENT 2 - 'Candidates with an Italian degree in classes different from those specified in Requisite 1 (for example: ex D.M. 270/04: L2 - Biotechnology, L13 - Biological Sciences or L9 - Industrial Engineering) but who have acquired the following CFU: at least 8 CFU in the subject areas: MAT/01 to 09; at least 6 CFU in the subject areas: FIS/01 to 08; at least 15 CFU in the subject areas: CHIM/01 to 07; at least 15 CFU in the subject areas: AGR/16, BIO/10, BIO/11, CHIM/11, ING-IND/25, ING-IND 27.' In plain terms: minimum 8 ECTS mathematics, 6 ECTS physics, 15 ECTS core chemistry (CHIM/01-07 covers analytical, physical, general/inorganic, organic, industrial and pharmaceutical chemistry) and 15 ECTS in the applied/bio cluster (agricultural chemistry AGR/16, biochemistry BIO/10, molecular biology BIO/11, chemistry for technologies CHIM/11, chemical plants ING-IND/25, industrial chemistry ING-IND/27). REQUIREMENT 3 - the route used by most international applicants: 'candidates with a foreign university degree (e.g., Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Biotechnology, Biology) with a curriculum corresponding, in terms of content, to requirements 1 or 2 indicated above.' Note the department's English page names the eligible foreign fields explicitly (Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Biotechnology, Biology) whereas the Italian regulation text is generic ('titolo universitario estero con curriculum corrispondente, per contenuto, ai requisiti 1 o 2'). TWO ADDITIONAL FILTERS published only on the live department page (they are NOT in the 2022 regulation): 'Students who obtained their last degree (BSc or MSc degree) not more that 7 years ago and had a graduation grade of 65% or high will be accepted for selection.' That is a 7-YEAR RECENCY LIMIT on the most recent degree and a MINIMUM GRADUATION GRADE OF 65% of the local scale. Applicants who graduated more than 7 years ago, or below 65%, are on the face of the published rule not accepted for the selection. MANDATORY IN ALL CASES: 'Verification of personal preparation is mandatory in all cases, and only students who meet the curricular requirements may enter' - i.e. the curricular requirements are a gate, not a substitute for the interview. Foreign qualifications must additionally be documented for the university's own recognition assessment (see required_documents). BACKGROUND-BASED TRACK ASSIGNMENT AFTER ADMISSION: because the cohort is deliberately mixed, 'The CCD will assign the students to each path based on their curriculum' - a chemistry-background student is routed to the Biology alignment path and vice versa.
entry_exam_or_test: NO written entrance examination and NO standardised test. There is no TOLC, no SAT, no GRE requirement and no unina.it-run admission exam for this programme. The admission decision rests on (1) a documentary screening by the CCD and (2) a compulsory ONLINE INTERVIEW. Regulation Art. 5, verbatim: 'I candidati all'iscrizione del corso di laurea che soddisfano i requisiti di ammissione sottopongono alla CCD il proprio curriculum. La CCD dopo verifica dei requisiti ammette i candidati alle prove di valutazione della preparazione personale.' SUBJECT SCOPE OF THE ASSESSMENT, verbatim: 'La valutazione vertera sulla conoscenza di base della matematica e della fisica oltre che la conoscenza approfondita della Chimica e delle discipline ad essa collegate' - i.e. basic mathematics and physics plus IN-DEPTH chemistry and related disciplines. FORMAT, verbatim: 'Le modalita di valutazione della preparazione personale e di individuazione del relativo percorso formativo sono definite annualmente dalla CCD e sono eseguite on line' - defined annually by the CCD and CARRIED OUT ONLINE. WHAT THE INTERVIEW ACTUALLY LOOKS LIKE, verbatim from the department page: 'The candidate will be contacted via e-mail for an on-line interview, where he/she will be asked to talk about the BSc thesis/final work, preparing a presentation using the attached template (see example) (max 5-6 min of talk), and for the verification of the documentation sent via e-mail.' So the candidate must prepare a SLIDE PRESENTATION on their bachelor thesis/final project using the department's own template, limited to roughly 5-6 minutes of speaking, and the same session is used to verify the uploaded documents. The slide deck is itself one of the documents that must be uploaded in advance in the merged application PDF. The Diploma Supplement or, alternatively, a Graduate Record Examination result is accepted as a transcript-equivalent document (GRE is listed as an ALTERNATIVE evidence document, not as a required admission test). The interview is scheduled by appointment: 'The candidates must compile the following module in order to get the appointment for the interview and to upload the necessary documents.' Note that the 3 CFU 'Additional language skills (Italian) or Further knowledge of computer science' slot and the two alignment paths are post-admission remedial/levelling devices, not entrance tests; there are no OFA (additional learning obligations) published for this programme.
seats_total: 30 (maximum). Verbatim and identically worded on two official unina.it sources: the orientamento.unina.it course profile ('Enrolment is limited to a maximum of 30 participants.') and the department's Student's Guide PDF ('Enrolment is limited to a maximum of 30 participants..'). The legal basis for capping is teaching regulation Art. 5: 'L'iscrizione al Corso di Laurea su decisione del CCD puo essere a numero chiuso' - the cap is set by the CCD, not by a ministerial numero programmato decree, so it can in principle be varied year to year by CCD resolution. This is a genuinely small cohort: 30 places across a joint Federico II / Politecnico di Torino degree. For context on real applicant volume, the official UNINA 'Study in Naples' scholarship ranking published on international.unina.it for A.Y. 2024/25 lists a competitive ICCBE-specific ranking of international candidates scored out of a maximum, with at least 17 ranked applicants named for scholarship purposes alone - indicating that the 30-place cap is meaningful rather than nominal.
non_eu_reserved_seats: NOT PUBLISHED [uncertain]. No unina.it source located in this research states a separate quota (contingente) of places reserved for non-EU candidates resident abroad for this programme. The published cap is a single undifferentiated figure - 'a maximum of 30 participants' - with no EU/non-EU split. This is consistent with the programme's access design: admission is by CCD screening plus interview rather than by a ranked national/ministerial competition, and the university's own international page confirms the non-EU route runs through Universitaly pre-enrolment plus the programme's own selection rather than through a reserved-seat ranking ('pre-enrolment alone does not grant admission to degree programmes. In order to matriculate you also need to take and pass the verifications of the entry requirements and the admission procedures set for the degree programme of your interest'). Federico II does publish explicit non-EU contingents for its nationally regulated numero programmato courses (Medicine and Surgery, Dentistry, Veterinary Medicine, Architecture) - ICCBE is not in that group. TREAT AS: no reserved non-EU quota published; non-EU applicants compete for the same 30 places. If a hard number is needed, it should be requested directly from iccbe@unina.it or read from the ministerial SUA-CdS sheet (linked by the department to https://www.universitaly.it/index.php/scheda/sua/59212, which is universitaly.it/MUR, outside the unina.it-only source scope of this research).
language_requirements: ENGLISH B2, CERTIFIED - and Italian NOT required. ENGLISH: the requirement is stated identically and unconditionally on the teaching regulation, the department page, the Student's Guide and the orientamento profile. Regulation Art. 4 (Italian): 'E richiesta una conoscenza certificata della lingua inglese di livello B2.' English pages: 'Certified English language proficiency at the B2 level is required.' B2 refers to the CEFR (Common European Framework of Reference) level. CRITICAL AND UNUSUAL CONCESSION - THE B2 CAN BE OBTAINED AFTER ENROLMENT: the department page states verbatim 'The B2 English language requirement can be achieved within the first year of the course (e.g., for academic year 22/23 it ends on March 31, 2024). Enrolled students can acquire B2 certification through the CLA (University Linguistic Center).' So a candidate without a certificate in hand at application time is not automatically excluded - the certificate may be obtained during the first year, with an in-house route through the Centro Linguistico di Ateneo (CLA). The worked example given (a.y. 2022/23 cohort had until 31 March 2024) implies a deadline of roughly 31 March of the SECOND calendar year of enrolment; the exact 2026/2027 cut-off date is not separately published. Applicants should note that 'English Certification' is nonetheless listed as one of the documents to be uploaded in the application PDF, so a certificate materially strengthens the application even though it can be completed later. NO SPECIFIC PROVIDER LIST OR SCORE TABLE is published by the programme - the department page does not enumerate accepted certificates or minimum IELTS/TOEFL scores. At university level, international.unina.it states that an international English certificate 'IELTS, TOEFL, Cambridge, etc.' is 'useful for the issue of the visa by the diplomatic/consular Representation' - i.e. the embassy will want it even where the programme allows deferral. ITALIAN: explicitly NOT required. international.unina.it, verbatim: 'If you choose a three-year, five-year or single-cycle degree course in ENGLISH, level B2 Italian language proficiency is not required.' (The B2 Italian requirement and the Italian proficiency test apply only to Italian-taught programmes.) Italian appears only as an optional 3 CFU curricular slot ('Additional language skills (Italian) or Further knowledge of computer science') and as free optional support: the CLA offers international students free ICoN self-study online Italian courses (icon-lingua.it) at A1 to C1 - 'Participation in the courses is free of charge and the licence is valid for one year' - with enrolment via a UNINA institutional e-mail address and a published annual registration deadline (20 November for the 2025/2026 round).
application_deadline_eu: OPENING DATE PUBLISHED, CLOSING DATE NOT PUBLISHED [uncertain]. WHAT IS OFFICIALLY STATED for A.Y. 2026/2027, verbatim on the live department page under 'Admission to the programme and prerequisites': 'The selections for A.Y. 2026/2027 will open on the 1st of March' - i.e. 2026-03-01. No closing date for the internal selection is published anywhere on the unina.it pages examined. DIRECT CONFLICT WITH THE DEPARTMENT'S OWN STUDENT'S GUIDE, which states under 'Application timeline': 'The call for applications is issued in late June and is posted on the website: www.scienzechimiche.unina.it/iccbe'. The Student's Guide is demonstrably stale on other points (it still names the previous Degree Programme Director), so the live page's 1 March opening should be preferred, but the late-June reference suggests selection activity continues into the summer. Consistent with a summer selection window, the department's own news slider advertises programme information sessions on 2 April 2026 at 14:00 and 23 July 2026 at 14:00, and previously 18 July 2025 at 12:00 - i.e. applicant-facing sessions spanning spring to late July. PRACTICAL GUIDANCE: EU and EU-treated candidates (Italian citizens, EU citizens wherever resident, and non-EU citizens legally resident in Italy or an EU country) do NOT use Universitaly and are bound only by the internal selection plus the university enrolment calendar. They should therefore apply as early as possible after 1 March 2026 and, in any case, well before the enrolment window closes. UNIVERSITY-LEVEL ENROLMENT CALENDAR FOR 2026/2027 (from the official 'Guida all'iscrizione Anno accademico 2026-27', dated 10/07/2026): '16 LUGLIO 2026 - Inizio periodo ordinario immatricolazione'; '1 SETTEMBRE 2026 - Inizio periodo ordinario iscrizione agli anni successivi'; '2 NOVEMBRE 2026 - Scadenza periodo ordinario immatricolazione e iscrizione agli anni successivi'. So the ORDINARY enrolment window is 16 July 2026 to 2 November 2026. Late enrolment is possible: from 3 November 2026 an extraordinary period opens; enrolment up to 15 January 2027 carries a EUR 50 surcharge and from 16 January 2027 a EUR 110 surcharge. A master-specific back-stop exists: 'Le iscrizioni al primo anno dei corsi di laurea magistrali potranno essere effettuate entro il 31 marzo 2027' - first-year enrolment in two-year master's programmes is possible up to 31 March 2027, but the same article warns that a CCD may require anyone enrolling after 31 December 2026 to first earn between 6 and 12 CFU through single-course enrolment. The guide itself cautions 'le date di scadenza possono essere soggette a variazioni'. VERIFY THE CLOSING DATE DIRECTLY with iccbe@unina.it before relying on any inferred date.
application_deadline_non_eu: TWO HARD UNIVERSITY-LEVEL DATES PLUS AN UNPUBLISHED PROGRAMME CLOSING DATE [uncertain]. NON-EU CANDIDATES RESIDENT ABROAD (visa needed) face a two-track timetable and the binding constraint is the Universitaly pre-enrolment date, which falls BEFORE the university's enrolment window even opens. Verbatim from international.unina.it: 'JUNE - 15 - 2026 - Pre-enrolment application deadline to University of Naples Federico II. After this date no programme changes are permitted. After this date pre-enrolment is allowed to the programmes with restricted access only.' and 'NOVEMBER - 30 - 2026 - Deadline for submitting the Visa Application at Iyalian [sic] Embassies /Consulates.' So: Universitaly pre-enrolment to Federico II by 2026-06-15; visa application at the Italian Embassy/Consulate by 2026-11-30. NOTE THE CARVE-OUT in the same sentence - after 15 June 2026 pre-enrolment remains open for restricted-access programmes; ICCBE is a restricted-access (numero chiuso by CCD decision) programme, which on the face of the wording may keep the Universitaly route open past 15 June, but this is an inference from a general rule and MUST be confirmed with the programme before being relied on. SEQUENCE THE NON-EU APPLICANT MUST FOLLOW: (1) complete the department's internal selection module and upload the merged PDF (selection opens 1 March 2026); (2) in parallel or afterwards, pre-enrol on Universitaly ('Application can be made both before and after the interview. It is mandatory to complete the application on Universitaly prior the deadline'); (3) sit the online interview; (4) on a positive outcome the pre-enrolment letter is uploaded by the department to Universitaly and the UNINA International Didactic Office validates the application; (5) apply for the type 'D' study visa ('studio - immatricolazione universita') at the named Embassy/Consulate; (6) enrol in person - foreign-citizenship students cannot use the online enrolment procedure ('Coloro che presentano una cittadinanza straniera dovranno effettuare l'iscrizione presso gli sportelli delle Segreterie Studenti, non potranno usare la procedura on-line'); (7) apply for a residence permit within 8 working days of entering Italy. VISA FINANCIAL THRESHOLD for 2026: proof of means of subsistence of EUR 10,179.85 per year, plus funds for repatriation, suitable accommodation and health insurance. NON-EU CANDIDATES WHO DO NOT NEED A VISA (non-EU citizens legally resident in Italy or an EU country) are exempt from Universitaly entirely: 'If you are a non-European student without the need for a visa and regularly residing in Italy with a regular study visa, you may present your academic documents directly to the Coordinator of the Course in which you wish to enrol. You will therefore not need to pre-register on the Universitaly Portal.' They follow the internal procedure only and the ordinary 16 July - 2 November 2026 enrolment window. WARNING: the university expressly states it does not issue admission letters for visa purposes and that pre-enrolment does not itself confer admission or any right to a visa.
required_documents: TWO DISTINCT DOCUMENT SETS - one for the programme selection, one for enrolment/visa. (A) FOR THE INTERNAL SELECTION - all documents must be merged into ONE PDF renamed Surname_Name.pdf and uploaded through the department's selection module; the department states categorically 'No documents sent in other form (e.g., via email) will be considered.' The published list, verbatim: 'Curriculum Vitae'; 'Bachelor Certificate'; 'Diploma Supplement or Graduate Record Examination'; 'Scan of the Passport'; 'English Certification'; 'Motivational letter'; 'Eventual Recommendation Letters'; 'Slide presentation for the interview using the attached template (see example)'. Notes: recommendation letters are optional ('eventual'); the Diploma Supplement may be replaced by a GRE result; the slide deck must use the department's own template and supports a 5-6 minute talk on the bachelor thesis/final work. (B) FOR RECOGNITION OF A FOREIGN QUALIFICATION (required by the university, per international.unina.it, and applicable to both EU and non-EU holders of foreign degrees): 'eventual translations'; 'legalisations'; 'Diploma Supplement'; 'certificates of examinations' / 'exam certificates'; 'certificates from the Italian ENIC NARIC centre (CIMEA)' (cimea.it - statement of comparability); 'any declarations of value issued by the competent diplomatic representations' (the Dichiarazione di Valore issued by the Italian Embassy). (C) FOR ENROLMENT (matriculation) at the Student Secretariat, per international.unina.it: 'Copy of passport'; 'Application form'; '1 passport photo'; 'Tax code' (codice fiscale - instructions published at international.unina.it); 'Residence permit (proof of having applied for it)'; 'Declaration of value issued by the Italian Embassy in the country where the degree was obtained or certificate of validity issued by ENIC-NARIC centres.' The page adds: 'Important: always check the instructions on the degree programme's website.' (D) FOR THE VISA APPLICATION at the Italian Embassy: the validated Universitaly pre-enrolment summary; any language competence certificates; health insurance policy; proof of financial means (EUR 10,179.85/year), repatriation funds and accommodation; plus the foreign-qualification documents. (E) FOR THE RESIDENCE PERMIT after arrival: passport copy including visa and entry stamp, SSN registration or health insurance, codice fiscale, proof of funds, accommodation documents, and either the UNINA enrolment certificate or the validated Universitaly pre-enrolment summary; a EUR 16 duty stamp plus post office fees (EUR 30.46 + EUR 40.00 + EUR 30 registered-letter charge). Contacts for help: iccbe@unina.it (programme), internationalwelcomedesk@unina.it (residence permit support), carmelamirella.secondulfo@unina.it and segrmmff@unina.it (student administration).
tuition_or_fees_link: PRIMARY LINKS: (1) Official 2026/2027 enrolment and fee guide - 'Guida all'iscrizione Anno accademico 2026-27' - https://www.unina.it/documents/d/guest/guida_studente_rapida_26-27_10-7-2026 (dated 10/07/2026); (2) index of student guides - https://www.unina.it/didattica/sportello-studenti/guide-dello-studente (the URL the programme itself cites for the 'Enrollment and Fee Payment Guide'); (3) official fee CALCULATOR/simulator - http://calcolatrice.unina.it/ (the guide states 'Per una simulazione degli importi da pagare vedi: http://calcolatrice.unina.it'); (4) university-level statement for international students - https://www.international.unina.it/education/admission-regulation/. HOW THE FEE IS DETERMINED: Federico II charges an income- and progress-based contribution, not a flat programme price. Verbatim: 'Il contributo per l'iscrizione viene determinato in funzione del reddito (ISEE Universitario) e della carriera (numero di cfu conseguiti e anno di iscrizione) di ciascuno studente.' FIRST-YEAR AMOUNTS FOR 2026/2027: exempt where the university ISEE (ISEEU) is up to EUR 30,000; otherwise a fixed component of EUR 1,011.50 plus a variable component, 'fino ad un massimo di 2.384,00 EUR per chi non presenta la dichiarazione ISEEU (ISEEU maggiore di 30.000 EUR)'. Above an ISEEU of EUR 80,000 amounts are no longer income-differentiated. REGIONAL RIGHT-TO-STUDY TAX 2026/2027 (compulsory, on top of the contribution, three bands): EUR 130.00 for ISEEU up to EUR 25,500 and for students from particularly poor countries (ex art. 13 c. 5 DPCM 9 April 2001, D.M. 176 of 24 February 2026); EUR 151.00 for ISEEU between EUR 25,500.01 and EUR 51,000 AND 'per gli studenti con nucleo familiare residente all'estero' (i.e. the band that normally applies to students whose family lives abroad); EUR 173.00 for ISEEU above EUR 51,000 and for anyone who files no ISEEU. Plus a EUR 16.00 stamp duty (imposta di bollo). THE TWO INTERNATIONAL CARVE-OUTS, verbatim from the 2026/27 guide's exemptions article: NON-EU CITIZENS - 'stranieri (cittadinanza in Paesi extra UE): sono esonerati totalmente dal pagamento del contributo di iscrizione; devono versare solo la tassa regionale per il diritto allo studio secondo le disposizioni di cui al punto 1 sopra e l'imposta di bollo' - i.e. non-EU citizens pay NO tuition contribution, only the regional tax (EUR 130/151/173) plus the EUR 16 stamp, so realistically about EUR 146-189 per year. OTHER-EU CITIZENS - 'europei (cittadinanza in altri Paesi UE): sono tenuti solo al versamento di un contributo fisso pari a 200 EUR per l'iscrizione, se l'importo del contributo dovuto sia pari o superiore a 200 EUR' - a flat EUR 200 contribution (plus regional tax and stamp), unless the ordinarily computed amount is lower. NOTE A STALE FIGURE: international.unina.it still summarises fees as 'European students EUR 200/year (tuition fees) + EUR 140/year regional tax (compulsory) + EUR 16.00 legal stamp' and 'Non-european students EUR 140/year regional fee (compulsory) + EUR 16.00 legal stamp'; the EUR 140 regional tax is superseded by the 2026/27 bands of EUR 130/151/173. INSTALMENTS 2026/2027: first instalment 60% of the amount + regional tax + stamp, payable from 16 July 2026 (or from 1 September) and by 2 November 2026; second instalment 20% by 1 March 2027; third instalment 20% by 30 April 2027; a EUR 100 surcharge applies from 16 July 2027 for unpaid 2nd/3rd instalments. REDUCTION RELEVANT TO THIS PROGRAMME: a 50% contribution reduction for first-year master's students who completed their Italian three-year bachelor by 31 October of their third year with a mark of 110 cum laude. FOREIGN-CITIZENSHIP STUDENTS MUST ENROL IN PERSON: 'Coloro che presentano una cittadinanza straniera dovranno effettuare l'iscrizione presso gli sportelli delle Segreterie Studenti, non potranno usare la procedura on-line.' SCHOLARSHIPS: ICCBE is one of the degree programmes listed in Table A of the university's 'Study in Naples' call (Federico II with Fondazione Compagnia di San Paolo), which for the 2024/25 round funded 26 two-year scholarships of EUR 11,059.92 gross each, ranked on career, motivation letter and language certification, with an ICCBE-specific published ranking; the calls and rankings are at https://www.international.unina.it/education/international-students-opportunities/ (as of this research the most recent call published there is 2024-2025, so the 2026/2027 call should be checked for publication). Right-to-study grants and accommodation are administered by A.Di.S.U.R.C. (via De Gasperi 45, Napoli). Students spending the third semester in Turin should budget separately for Turin accommodation (POLITO Welcome@PoliTO pages) and for the EUR 16 stamp duty on the POLITO attendance certificate.

uncertainty_notes: 1) DEGREE CLASS CODE CONFLICT (flagged uncertain). orientamento.unina.it, updated for a.y. 2026/2027, gives 'LM-71 R'; the teaching regulation, the Manifesto and the Student's Guide all give plain 'LM-71'. The regulation dates from 31/01/2022 and predates the D.M. 1649/2023 class reform, so the 'R' is almost certainly a straightforward re-coding of the same class rather than a different programme - but no unina.it document was found that explicitly states the transition for this course, and no reformed (post-2023) teaching regulation for ICCBE was located. Use LM-71 R for a 2026/2027 application and treat LM-71 as its pre-reform equivalent. 2) NO PUBLISHED CLOSING DATE FOR THE SELECTION (flagged uncertain). The live department page publishes only the OPENING date ('The selections for A.Y. 2026/2027 will open on the 1st of March'). No closing date appears anywhere on the department page, the orientamento profile or the unina.it course card. The Student's Guide contradicts the opening date by saying the call 'is issued in late June'. The department's news slider shows applicant information sessions on 2 April 2026 and 23 July 2026, which suggests rolling interview rounds through the summer rather than a single cut-off. The application form itself (a Google Form linked from the official page) could not be read during this research and may carry a date. ACTION: confirm the closing date with iccbe@unina.it. 3) NON-EU RESERVED SEATS NOT PUBLISHED (flagged uncertain). The 30-place cap is undifferentiated; no EU/non-EU split was found on any unina.it page. This should not be read as 'zero reserved seats' but as 'no quota published'. 4) UNIVERSITALY 15 JUNE 2026 DEADLINE AND THE RESTRICTED-ACCESS CARVE-OUT (flagged uncertain within the non-EU deadline field). international.unina.it says that after 15 June 2026 'pre-enrolment is allowed to the programmes with restricted access only'. ICCBE IS a restricted-access programme, so on a literal reading its Universitaly window may extend past 15 June - but this is an inference from a general university rule, not a programme-specific statement, and the safe course is to pre-enrol by 15 June 2026. 5) NO STANDALONE ADMISSION BANDO (flagged uncertain in official_call_url). There is no numbered call or rectoral decree for ICCBE admission; the department website is the call, and the actual application channel is a third-party Google Form linked from the unina.it page. This is unusual for an Italian degree and means the published rules can change without a dated document trail. 6) THE STUDENT'S GUIDE PDF IS STALE and should not be used as the primary source: it names Prof. Martino Di Serio as Degree Programme Director and Prof. Roberta Marchetti as international-students contact, whereas the live site names Prof. Vincenzo Russo for both; it also gives the 'late June' call timing and a 'September 1 to October 31' enrolment window that the 2026/27 university guide supersedes (16 July - 2 November 2026). 7) THE international.unina.it FEE PARAGRAPH IS STALE: it still quotes a EUR 140/year regional tax, superseded by the 2026/2027 bands of EUR 130 / 151 / 173 in the official Guida all'iscrizione 2026-27. Also note the international page's typo 'Iyalian Embassies' and 'Eropean students'. 8) THE REGULATION CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON THE PROGRAMME NAME: Art. 1 twice writes 'Industrial Chemistry for Circular Economy' (omitting 'and Bio') while the header and every public page use 'Industrial Chemistry for Circular and Bio Economy'. The full form is operative; the diploma name is the English title, with 'Chimica Industriale per l'Economia Circolare e la Bioeconomia' as the parallel Italian denomination. 9) STUDY PLAN VERSION LAG: the orientamento page is stamped 'Updated on a.y. 2026/2027' but its downloadable study plans are labelled 'Study plan 2025/2026' and 'Study plan 2024/2025', and the Manifesto on scuolapsb.unina.it is the 2024/2025 edition carrying the 'PIANO DEGLI STUDI A.A. 2022-2023' table. The credit structure quoted in this file is the one published on the 2026/2027-stamped orientamento page and matches the Student's Guide, but a 2026/2027-specific plan PDF was not located. 10) JOINT-DEGREE PRACTICALITIES ARE A REAL COST FACTOR not reflected in the Federico II fee figures: one semester in Turin means separate accommodation and living costs in a higher-cost northern city; the department's 'Staying at PoliTO' section acknowledges this by pointing to POLITO accommodation services and Turin transport discounts.
